```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(coherentSurv)
```

This tutorial uses constructed records only. Mapping a table establishes a data
contract; it does not establish complete ascertainment, independent censoring,
causal identification or regulatory compliance.

## Selected ADTTE endpoint

Select one endpoint parameter before fitting. Preserve the supplied duration
definition. Declare which censor codes represent events and which represent
censoring; subtracting CNSR from one is incorrect for multi-code censoring.

```{r adam}
adtte <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("001", "1", "003"), PARAMCD = "OS",
                    AVAL = c(5, 8, 10), CNSR = c(0L, 1L, 2L))
adsl <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("001", "1", "003"), age = c(51, 62, 47))
history <- cs_from_adam(adtte, paramcd = "OS", event_codes = 0,
  censor_codes = c(1, 2), time_unit = "days",
  duration_definition = "Constructed elapsed follow-up in days",
  ascertainment = "Complete endpoint follow-up by construction",
  provenance = "Synthetic tutorial; no patient records",
  adsl = adsl, covariates = "age")
history[, c("id", "start", "stop", "terminal", "age")]
stopifnot(identical(history$id, c("001", "1", "003")),
          identical(history$terminal, c(1L, 0L, 0L)))
```

The adapter requires one selected endpoint row per person. The analyst must
justify the endpoint and time origin. It does not turn a single-endpoint ADTTE
extract into unobserved recurrent histories.

## Reviewed OMOP-style extract

Real OMOP date fields often coarsen event times. This example explicitly assumes
events at exact day boundaries, one continuous observation period per person,
and a process origin equal to its start. Use this mapping only when those
assumptions are justified. Ambiguous same-day ordering needs a separate
coarsening model; the adapter never adds jitter.

```{r omop}
origin <- as.Date("2020-01-01")
person <- data.frame(person_id = c("001", "1"))
period <- data.frame(person_id = person$person_id,
  observation_period_start_date = origin,
  observation_period_end_date = origin + 10)
events <- data.frame(person_id = c("001", "1"),
  condition_concept_id = c("EXAMPLE_A", "EXAMPLE_A"),
  condition_start_date = origin + c(3, 4))
death <- data.frame(person_id = "001", death_date = origin + 8)
mapped <- cs_from_omop(person, period, events,
  concept_map = c(EXAMPLE_A = "episode"), origin = rep(origin, 2),
  time_unit = "days", timing = "exact_day_boundaries",
  ascertainment = "Continuous complete ascertainment by construction",
  provenance = "Artificial source labels; not real standard OMOP concepts",
  death = death)
mapped[, c("id", "start", "stop", "event_type", "terminal")]
stopifnot(sum(mapped$.cs_mark > 0) == 2, sum(mapped$terminal) == 1)
```

The supplied concept map must have been reviewed for the actual study. Table
presence alone cannot establish that all episodes or deaths were observed.
Multiple observation periods, delayed entry and unknown event counts are not
reconstructed by this adapter. Source-row mappings stay with the local object;
the audit export includes declared mapping rules but omits subject-level origins.

## Scientific declarations and provenance

For a treatment-effect analysis, define the population, treatment conditions,
endpoint, intercurrent-event strategy and population-level summary in advance.
`cs_fit()` and `cs_causal()` retain an optional `estimand` declaration. This
metadata does not select new estimands or make observational effects identified.
The causal entry point still requires its documented baseline binary-treatment
and observation assumptions.

```{r audit}
audit <- cs_audit_report(history, include_session = FALSE)
audit$model$mapping_provenance$adapter
audit$export$data_fingerprint$algorithm
```

Hashes compare the specified bytes. They are not anonymization, a protected
record history, a digital signature or an immutable archive. Review free-text
labels and paths before sharing an audit report.

## Offline diagnostic checks

```{r environment}
diagnostic <- cs_validate_env()
diagnostic$checks[, c("check", "status", "maximum_absolute_error")]
stopifnot(identical(diagnostic$operational_status, "passed"))
```

Four small analytic references check the Poisson boundary likelihood, dense and
sparse absorbing-state propagation, and Louis mixture information. Unavailable
compiler provenance remains unavailable; a compiler currently on PATH is not
proof of which compiler built the installed binary. The optional `timings=TRUE`
records elapsed fixture times and returned-object sizes, not peak memory or
comparative throughput. JSON/text reports are unsigned diagnostics, not formal
IQ/OQ/PQ qualification or FDA, NIH or NHS certification.

All these runtime examples are offline once R, coherentSurv and its dependencies
are installed. Air-gapped installation requires staging those dependencies and
the appropriate toolchain separately.

## Python and workflow conditions

The installed `python/run_rpy2.py` example fits once and retains its R object.
`--verify-parity` deliberately adds a second fit to compare direct-R transport;
`--timings` records stages. `python/run_forecast.py` offers an Rscript route.
These examples use the same R/C++ engine, not an independent Python model.

Errors raised by the R validation helpers inherit a specific `cs_error_<code>`
class and the broad `coherentSurv_error` class. For example, code can handle
`cs_error_interval` without searching error-message text. A nonregular ordinary
fit raises `cs_warning_nonregular_fit`; reporting methods withhold unsupported
Wald intervals. Native/system errors can still use their underlying classes.
